newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus falls 91.7 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus falls 91.7 pct in January.

text.p: Japan"s customs-cleared trade surplus fell 91.7 percent in January from a year earlier to 5.19 billion yen, the 26th consecutive month of year-on-year declines, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
The trade surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, rose 81.6 percent in January from a year earlier to 298.34 billion yen. The figures were not adjusted for seasonal factors.

Economists had been deeply divided in their forecasts for the figures due to seasonal factors and they said January figures are a poor guide to changes in Japan"s trade patterns. Forecasts had ranged from a deficit of 190 billion yen ($1.53 billion) to a surplus of 150 billion yen ($1.20 billion).

But many economists said they expect the yen"s fall since mid-1995 to boost exports, while discouraging imports, eventually causing a halt in the trend of a declining surplus. A weaker yen makes Japanese products cheaper in terms of foreign currency.

The Bank of Japan, the nation"s central bank, said on Tuesday that Japan"s trade surplus has been rising in real terms since last autumn. Car exports, especially to the United States, are surging, pushing up the overall trade surplus.
